subject: Zero-Trust proxy binding for private endpoints — operational checklist
messages:
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, samira@catalysthealth.com
Cc: michael.ortega@catalysthealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zero-Trust proxy binding for private endpoints — operational checklist

Hi all,

Following up from yesterday's call — Catalyst's security team asked us for a concise, operational checklist that describes how Redwood will bind a private endpoint to Catalyst's NAT/proxy in a zero-trust-friendly way. Samira, thanks for the clear notes on their side.

I've drafted a proposal (attached) and want to validate it with David (runtime/networks) and Laura (customer ops). High-level goals:
- Minimal outbound surface: single egress IP or small CIDR for the control plane connector; prefer TLS with cert pinning.
- No long-lived firewall exceptions: we will suggest ephemeral IPs with rotation policy and a short escalation window.
- mTLS for control-plane handshake and an operator concierge flow for short-lived registration.

Requesting:
1) David — quick feasibility check on the runtime side (ports, SNI bindings, expected SNI fingerprint behavior with current proxies).
2) Laura — propose an ops playbook for oncall and canary cutover.
3) Samira/Michael — confirm any procurement or JML constraints on your side (e.g., IP allowlisting timelines, change windows).

I've attached: proxy-binding-checklist.pdf (living checklist), catalyst-network-diagram.png (their sketch), mtls-cert-exchange-sample.txt (example curl commands).

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, samira@catalysthealth.com
Cc: michael.ortega@catalysthealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zero-Trust proxy binding for private endpoints — operational checklist

Jordan / team — quick pass from runtime/infra: checklist looks solid overall. A few clarifications and constraints below. I'll call out action items inline.

1) Egress surface: we can present either a single static IP (managed NAT) or a short-lived egress pool (ephemeral NAT with rotation). For Catalyst I recommend a small /29 sized pool if they insist on IP-based allowlists; this gives us headroom for ephemeral rotation without breaking the firewall. Action: Samira, confirm if a /29 is acceptable or if strictly 1 IP is required.

2) mTLS and certificate pinning: we support client cert authentication on the connector. The control plane TLS SNI will be stable (hostname: control.redwood-internal.net), but note that some corporate proxies will re-write SNI for outbound inspection — that breaks SNI fingerprinting. If Catalyst uses an outbound TLS inspector, we need to fall back to mutual TLS cert checks and a signed device assertion we push during the registration handshake. Action: Samira — are you running TLS inspection on outbound? If yes we will provide the certificate chain and an alternate cert-assertion flow.

3) Ports and protocols: We require outbound TCP 443 for control plane and optionally TCP 5671 (AMQP) only when using kafka-style telemetry forwarding. Recommend customers keep 443 open and avoid special ports. Action: Jordan to confirm the customer will not request nonstandard ports for runtime.

4) DNS split-horizon: For deterministic routing we expect customers to resolve our control hostname to the egress IP(s) we provide. If Catalyst runs internal split-horizon DNS, we'll provide both A records and TXT metadata for validation. Action: Samira, provide the DNS admin contact and preferred TTL.

5) Emergency fallback: We'll pre-authorize a limited "maintenance" public fallback (hosted proxy) reachable from any IP, but gated by a short-lived token and step-up MFA from Catalyst operators. This is for urgent operations only and will be documented in the playbook.

6) Canary plan: We need a 15-minute canary where a single tenant's traffic is routed to the new binding while observability is monitored (token logs, p50/p95 latency, error rates).

I'll attach a minimal runbook note to the checklist for Laura.

-David

--
David Kim
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: samira@catalysthealth.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: michael.ortega@catalysthealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-Trust proxy binding for private endpoints — operational checklist

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple of constraints from our security/compliance team:

- We cannot open any inbound ports. Outbound 443 is fine but must be restricted to the list you give us. We cannot accept ephemeral CIDRs that rotate more frequently than 24h unless we are notified with a signed list 24h prior.
- We do perform TLS inspection at the perimeter. We'll need the cert pinning + signed device assertion approach you mentioned. We can host your cert chain in our vault (HashiCorp) if you provide the thumbprint and rotation policy.
- Change window: firewall changes require a 48h lead time for our SREs. Small exceptions can be handled during our maintenance window: Sat 02:00–04:00 local.

Action items on our side:
1) I'll open a request ticket with our firewall team and copy David in the request. Expect a ticket number by EOD.
2) Michael will coordinate the DNS admin and share contact info.

One more ask: can you provide a short signed statement (PDF) listing the security controls on the connector (mTLS, mutual auth, telemetry retention window, purge policy)? We need that for our vendor review pack.

Samira
Director, Cloud Security
Catalyst Health
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, samira@catalysthealth.com
Cc: michael.ortega@catalysthealth.com
Date: Sun, 31 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-Trust proxy binding for private endpoints — operational checklist

Great thread — summary and next steps below. I've translated David/Samira constraints into a short ops playbook for the canary and handoff. See bullets for owners and ETA.

Summary (one-liner): Redwood will use mutual TLS plus a signed device assertion for control-plane binding; Catalyst will allow outbound TCP/443 to the provided egress IP pool (/29 preferred) with a 48h change window.

Playbook (canary & handoff):
- Prework (Jordan) — collect procurement dates and open the firewall ticket on Catalyst side. ETA: 2028-04-02 (Jordan/Samira).
- Connector config (David) — prepare connector build with client cert, rotation set to 24h, and a signed device-assertion endpoint. Push config to staging and provide sample curl flows. ETA: 2028-04-04.
- Signed controls statement (Security docs) — I'll draft a 1-page statement (mTLS, telemetry retention 30d, access audit logs 365d) and route to legal for signature. ETA: 2028-04-03.
- Canary (Operations) — target window: Sat 2028-04-07 02:15–02:45 PST (fits Catalyst maintenance). Scope: single tenant test, health checks, rollback threshold: >1% error or >2x baseline p95. Owner: Laura (runbook) with David on-call.

Attachments I'll push to the shared drive: a brief runbook and a single-sheet controls statement stub. Jordan — can you confirm the procurement milestone so I can lock the dates?

I'll be oncall that weekend and will coordinate the cutover.

Thanks everyone — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Customer Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
